items.title: Perfection Supplied by Others Completes, and the Third Favourable Condition Opens: A Genuine Wish for the Good

items.zh: 他謂施主。彼於行者起哀愍心，惠施隨順淨命資具，所謂如法衣服、飲食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥。如是名為他所哀愍。云何善法欲？謂如有一，或從佛所、或弟子所，聞正法已，獲得淨信。得淨信已，應如是學：在家煩擾，若居塵宇，出家閑曠，猶處虛空，是故我今應捨一切妻子眷屬、財穀珍寶，於善說法毘奈耶中，正捨家法，趣於非家。既出家已，勤修正行，令得圓滿。於善法中生如是欲，名善法欲。
items.en: "Others" means benefactors. Giving rise to compassion for the practitioner, they bestow the requisites that support a pure livelihood — namely, robes, food, seat and bedding, and medicine for illness, all rightly obtained. This is called being shown compassion by others. What is a genuine wish for the good? It is like one who, having heard the true Dharma from the Buddha or from his disciples, attains pure faith. Having attained this pure faith, one should train thus: household life is troubled and vexing, like dwelling in a dust-filled dwelling; going forth is open and spacious, like abiding in open space. Therefore I should now relinquish my spouse, children, kin, wealth, grain, and treasures, and, within this well-taught Dharma and discipline, rightly relinquish the householder's way and go forth into homelessness. Having thus gone forth, one diligently cultivates correct practice, bringing it to completion. Giving rise to such a wish within what is wholesome is called a genuine wish for the good.

items.title: Formal Ordination, and the Six Components of Moral Discipline

items.zh: 云何正出家？謂即由此勝善法欲增上力故，白四羯磨，受具足戒；或受勞策所學尸羅。是名正出家。云何戒律儀？謂彼如是正出家已，安住具戒，堅牢防護別解律儀，軌則、所行皆得圓滿，於微小罪見大怖畏，受學一切所有學處。是名戒律儀。
items.en: What is proper going-forth? It is that, by the power of this excellent wish for the good, one undergoes the formal act of ordination and receives the full precepts; or receives the training precepts of a novice. This is called proper going-forth. What is moral discipline in its proper restraint? It is that, having thus properly gone forth, one abides in complete discipline, firmly guarding the prātimokṣa restraint, perfecting both protocol and proper conduct, seeing great danger in even the slightest fault, and training in every one of the points of training. This is called moral discipline in its proper restraint.

items.title: Guarding the Senses: Neither Grasping the Whole Nor Its Alluring Details

items.zh: 云何根律儀？謂即依此尸羅律儀，守護正念，修常委念，以念防心，行平等位。眼見色已，而不取相，不取隨好。恐依是處，由不修習眼根律儀防護而住，其心漏泄所有貪憂惡不善法。故即於彼修律儀行，防護眼根，依於眼根修律儀行。如是行者，耳聞聲已、鼻嗅香已、舌甞味已、身覺觸已、意了法已，而不取相，不取隨好。恐依是處，由不修習意根律儀防護而住。其心漏泄所有貪憂惡不善法。故即於彼修律儀行，防護意根，依於意根修律儀行。是名根律儀。
items.en: What is restraint of the faculties? It is that, resting on this discipline and restraint, one guards correct mindfulness, cultivates constant and thoroughgoing mindfulness, protects the mind by means of mindfulness, and dwells in equanimity. Having seen a form with the eye, one does not grasp its general mark, nor its alluring details — fearing that, by not cultivating restraint and protection of the eye faculty in this respect, the mind might leak out craving, distress, and other unwholesome states. One therefore cultivates restraint precisely with regard to this, guarding the eye faculty, and practising restraint in reliance on the eye faculty. In just the same way, having heard a sound with the ear, smelled a scent with the nose, tasted a flavour with the tongue, felt a touch with the body, or cognized a mental object with the mind, one does not grasp its general mark, nor its alluring details. …One therefore cultivates restraint precisely with regard to this, guarding the mind faculty, and practising restraint in reliance on the mind faculty. This is called restraint of the faculties.

items.title: Moderation in Eating, and Wakefulness Through the Watches of the Night

items.zh: 云何於食知量？謂彼如是守諸根已，以正思擇食於所食。不為倡蕩、不為憍逸、不為飾好、不為端嚴食於所食。然食所食，為身安住、為暫支持、為除飢渴、為攝梵行、為斷故受、為令新受當不更生、為當存養力樂無罪安隱而住。如是名為於食知量。云何初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽？謂彼如是食知量已，於晝日分，經行、宴坐二種威儀，從順障法淨修其心；於初夜分，經行、宴坐二種威儀，從順障法淨修其心。過此分已，出住處外，洗濯其足，右脇而臥，重累其足，住光明想、正念、正知、思惟起想。於夜後分，速疾覺寤，經行、宴坐二種威儀，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: What is moderation in eating? It is that, having thus guarded the faculties, one eats with correct discernment. One does not eat for the sake of wanton pleasure, nor for pride and indulgence, nor to enhance one's beauty, nor for physical elegance. Rather, one eats so that the body may be sustained, so as to provide temporary support, so as to remove hunger and thirst, so as to uphold the pure conduct of one's practice, so as to end old feelings [of discomfort], so that new feelings [of discomfort] will not arise, and so as to preserve strength, ease, and a blameless, peaceful abiding. This is called moderation in eating. What is diligently cultivating wakeful yogic practice through the first and last watches of the night? It is that, having thus practised moderation in eating, during the day, through the two postures of walking meditation and sitting meditation, one purifies the mind of whatever obstructs it; …once this period ends, one goes outside one's dwelling, washes the feet, lies down on the right side, one foot resting upon the other, dwelling in the perception of light, with correct mindfulness, correct awareness, and the intention to rise. In the last watch of the night, one wakes swiftly, and through walking meditation and sitting meditation, purifies the mind of whatever obstructs it.

items.zh: 如是名為初夜後夜常勤修習覺寤瑜伽。

items.title: Clear Awareness in Every Activity, and the Delight of Genuine Solitude

items.zh: 云何正知而住？謂彼如是常勤修習覺寤瑜伽已，若往、若來正知而住，若覩、若瞻正知而住，若屈、若伸正知而住，持僧伽胝及以衣鉢正知而住，若食、若飲、若噉、若嘗正知而住，若行、若住、若坐、若臥正知而住，於覺寤時正知而住，若語、若默正知而住，如解勞睡時正知而住。如是名為正知而住。云何樂遠離？謂由如是所修善法，無倒修治初業地已，遠離一切臥具貪著，住阿練若、樹下、空室、山谷峯穴、草藉、逈露、塚間、林藪、虛曠平野、邊際臥具。是名樂遠離。
items.en: What is clear awareness in activity? It is that, having thus diligently practised wakeful yogic discipline, one maintains clear awareness whether going or coming, whether looking afar or looking near, whether bending or extending a limb, while carrying the great robe, bowl, and other robes, while eating, drinking, chewing, or tasting, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, while awake, whether speaking or silent, and even while resting from fatigue. This is called clear awareness in activity. What is delight in solitude? It is that, by means of the wholesome states thus cultivated, having rightly trained the foundational stage of practice without error, one relinquishes all attachment to bedding, [whether fine or poor,] and dwells in a forest retreat, beneath a tree, in an empty room, a mountain valley, a mountain cave, a heap of grass, an open clearing, a charnel ground, a thicket, or a vast open plain, using only the barest bedding. This is called delight in solitude.

items.title: Purifying the Five Hindrances: The Eleventh Favourable Condition

items.zh: 云何清淨諸蓋？謂彼如是住阿練若，或復樹下，或空室等，於五種蓋淨修其心。所謂貪欲、瞋恚、惛沈睡眠、掉舉惡作、及以疑蓋。從彼諸蓋淨修心已，心離諸蓋，安住賢善勝三摩地。如是名為清淨諸蓋。
items.en: What is purifying the hindrances? It is that, dwelling thus in a forest retreat, beneath a tree, in an empty room, or the like, one purifies the mind of the five hindrances — namely, sensual craving, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt. Having purified the mind of these hindrances, the mind, free of the hindrances, abides in an excellent and wholesome concentration.

blocks.text: The remaining lesser conditions describe the disciple's daily training, item by item. These items will be expanded in great detail in the following fascicles, so today is an overview.
The "wish for the good" (善法欲) arises from pure faith. Master Cháng Bǎi: the practitioner wishes to accord with the good, and so goes forth.

By the power of this wish one is ordained and receives the precepts. Master Cháng Bǎi: after one announcement and three formal motions, one becomes a full monk or nun. Moral discipline has six components (as on Day 132). The **restraint of individual liberation** (prātimokṣa): Master Cháng Bǎi: each precept frees one from the affliction it addresses.
Seeing a form, one grasps "neither its overall mark nor its alluring details". Master Cháng Bǎi: neither the coarse overall appeal nor the fine particular appeal. Its key is the mind faculty.

One eats "not for pleasure, pride, or beauty", but so that the body may be sustained for the holy life. One sleeps in the middle watch only. Master Cháng Bǎi: from 9 p.m. to 3 a.m., six hours. And one sleeps with the thought of rising: "if you think this inwardly, the ālayavijñāna records it, and you wake when the time comes."
"One maintains clear awareness whether going or coming, looking far or near, bending or extending a limb, speaking or silent." Then one delights in solitude: a quiet dwelling, simple bedding.

The five hindrances: sensual craving, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt. Master Cháng Bǎi adds a modern caution: for someone already depressed, impurity meditation may not suit; loving-kindness or recollection of the Buddha's qualities may be better.

quiz.q: How does "a genuine wish for the good" arise, and what implicit intent does it carry, per the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: it comes from pure faith; Cháng Bǎi: its hidden intent is encouraging ordination — household life like a dusty dwelling, renunciation like open space
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: where does the wish for the good come from? From pure faith. Master Cháng Bǎi: the practitioner wishes to accord with the good; another hidden intent is encouraging ordination. The treatise: household life is troubled, like a dusty dwelling; going forth is spacious, like open space.

quiz.q: What is the "fourfold formal act" (白四羯磨), per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: one announcement followed by three formal proposals, after which one is a full monk or nun
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after one announcement and three formal proposals, one becomes a full monk or nun. Venerable Miào Jìng: first one takes a teacher and novice precepts, then receives the monk's precepts by the fourfold act — the full precepts.

quiz.q: In "not grasping the general mark or its alluring details," how do the masters distinguish the two?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the mark is the coarse overall appeal, details the fine particular appeal; Miào Jìng: the mark is the large feature, details the small ones around it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing a form, one grasps neither the coarse overall appeal nor the fine particular appeal. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "mark" is the large feature; the "details" are the small features around it.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how does one eat with moderation?
options: not for wanton pleasure, pride, beauty, or elegance, but to sustain the body, support it, remove hunger, uphold the holy life
quiz.why: "One does not eat for the sake of wanton pleasure, nor for pride and indulgence, nor to enhance one's beauty… Rather, one eats so that the body may be sustained… so as to remove hunger and thirst, so as to uphold the pure conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: eating only a sesame seed and a grain of wheat, one might starve in three days — too little also prevents practice.

quiz.q: Wakeful yoga is practised in the first and last watches, sleeping in the middle watch. When is the middle watch, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: 9 p.m. to 3 a.m. — a practitioner sleeps only six hours
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the middle watch is from 9 p.m. to 3 a.m.; a practitioner sleeps only six hours.

quiz.q: How do the masters distinguish 覩 and 瞻?
options: 覩 is looking afar, 瞻 looking near
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 覩 is looking afar, 瞻 looking near; whether far or near, one abides in clear awareness. Venerable Miào Jìng: 睹 is looking from a distance; 瞻 is close observation.

quiz.q: Which five hindrances does the treatise say must be purified?
options: sensual craving, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, doubt
quiz.why: "Namely, sensual craving, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt." Master Cháng Bǎi: among all afflictions, sensual craving is the strongest.
